nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number. A group $H$ is $p$-local when, for every natural number $n$ coprime to $p$, the map $x \mapsto x^n$ is a bijection of $H$.
nodes.title: $p$-local groups

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number. A homomorphism of groups $e \colon G \to L$ is a $p$-localization when $L$ is nilpotent and $p$-local, and every homomorphism $f$ from $G$ to a nilpotent $p$-local group $H$ factors uniquely through $e$: there is exactly one homomorphism $g \colon L \to H$ with $g \circ e = f$.
nodes.title: $p$-localization of a group
